verbalization: Arcyroxocin B-6-O-Sulfate is proposed to interact with EDD domain protein, DegV family through a mechanistic pathway involving the induction of myeloid leukemia cell differentiation protein Mcl-1. The drug is known to target Mcl-1, a key regulator of cell survival and proliferation in leukemic cells. Mcl-1 is a substrate of the enzyme (6aR,11aR)-9-hydroxy-3-methoxy-6a,11a-dihydro-6H-[1]benzofuro[3,2-c]chromene-2-carbaldehyde, which is itself a target of Arcyroxocin B-6-O-Sulfate. This enzyme likely modulates Mcl-1 levels, promoting its degradation and thereby inducing differentiation in myeloid leukemia cells. The EDD domain protein, DegV family, is a known target of Mcl-1, and its interaction with Arcyroxocin B-6-O-Sulfate is inferred through the observed pathway. The evidence suggests a direct, mechanistic link between the drug and the EDD domain protein, supported by the drug’s ability to influence Mcl-1 levels and its known mode of action. The relationship is further supported by the presence of a final score of 0.6018, indicating a plausible and well-supported pathway.
